headline: High-risk filesystem and browser-enabled coding agent paired with a broad-egress travel planner creates medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; plano has broad network egress and consumes config/API inputs. If plano outputs are copied into Cline’s workspace or MCP-fed, malicious content can steer tool use. The shared filesystem path makes this plausible, though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF plano output is placed into a Cline-readable workspace file
IF an MCP server relays plano content into Cline without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep plano outputs out of shared files
Disable MCP bridges between the agents
Use a read-only handoff file for any transfer
Add a provenance header to every transferred artifact
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitizing wrappers on shared channels

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and can write workspace files; plano handles logs, traces, and metrics and has broad egress. A shared workspace or copied artifacts can move sensitive code or operational data between them, and plano’s API-backed processing increases leakage surface. The profiles do not prove default sharing, so medium is the highest justified level.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace directory
IF source code or screenshots are copied into plano inputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Avoid placing screenshots or secrets in shared folders
Redact logs before handing them to plano
Restrict plano to non-sensitive test data
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted workspace write and modify_git_state, while plano can read config files and has broad egress. Cline’s shared_state_with_other_instances is via filesystem, so concurrent writes to the same repo or config can race and corrupt git state. Because the write overlap is explicit and defaults are not isolated, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or config directory
IF Cline and plano run concurrently without file locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use separate branches for each agent
Lock shared files during edits
Keep plano read-only on shared repos
requires-engineering: add workspace-level mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code or browser-derived facts, and plano can consume API inputs and route outputs. If plano treats Cline’s artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream routing or planning decisions. The profiles do not show explicit verification between them, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF plano ingests Cline-produced files or summaries as trusted input
IF no verification step checks Cline’s claims before plano acts
mitigations: Require human review before handoff
Add checksum or schema validation on transferred artifacts
Use a second-pass verifier for critical outputs
Limit plano to advisory-only mode
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware orchestration

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys; plano handles logs, traces, and metrics. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible. Because the other agent is not clearly implicated in a specific regulated-data flow, one citation per agent is sufficient here.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cline screenshots or plano logs
IF retention policies differ for the same data class
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Set short log retention
Mask secrets before capture
Document data-class handling per agent
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
